\section*{Question 4}

The graph of a differentiable function \(f\) on the closed interval [-3,15] is shown in the figure above. The graph of \(f\) has a horizontal tangent line at \(x=6\). Let \(g(x)=5+\int_{6}^{x} f(t) d t\) for \(-3 \leq x \leq 15\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find \(g(6), g^{\prime}(6)\), and \(g^{\prime \prime}(6)\).
\item[(b)] On what intervals is \(g\) decreasing? Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] On what intervals is the graph of \(g\) concave down? Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] Find a trapezoidal approximation of \(\int_{-3}^{15} f(t) d t\) using six subintervals of length \(\Delta t=3\).
\item[(a)] \(\quad g(6)=5+\int_{6}^{6} f(t) d t=5\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& g^{\prime}(6)=f(6)=3 \\
& g^{\prime \prime}(6)=f^{\prime}(6)=0
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(b)] \(g\) is decreasing on [-3, 0] and [12, 15] since \(g^{\prime}(x)=f(x)<0\) for \(x<0\) and \(x>12\).
\item[(c)] The graph of \(g\) is concave down on \((6,15)\) since \(g^{\prime}=f\) is decreasing on this interval.
\end{itemize}
\[
\begin{array}{r|r|r|r|r|}
\hline & 3 \\
\hline & 2 & & & \\
\hline & 0 & & & \\
\hline & & & & \\
\hline & 3 & & & \\
\hline
\end{array}
\]
\[
3\left\{\begin{array}{l}
1: g(6) \\
1: g^{\prime}(6) \\
1: g^{\prime \prime}(6)
\end{array}\right.
\]
